title: Why does the Qur'an use the death-verb for sleep?

beats.narration: One Arabic verb — yatawaffā, to take in full — does two jobs in this verse: dying, and falling asleep. Why the same word for both?
Notice what it doesn't say: not that sleep resembles death, but that one verb performs both. Then it forks — He holds one self back, and sends the other on until an appointed term.
Okay — here's where it gets interesting. 6:60 runs the same scene with a bolder verb: baʿatha, the resurrection word, used for waking up in the morning.

So sleep is spoken of in the language of death, and waking in the language of resurrection. The most we can fairly say is this: the proof offered for being raised again isn't exotic — it's last night.
